titleEn: Idghām Kabīr Mutaqārībān in two words
description:
This section talks about the rules when idghām kabīr mutaqārībān occurs in a two words. (ie the mudgham is at the end of the first word and the mudgham fῑh is at the beginning of the next word. For a description of these terms see the previous section on idghām kabīr mithlān in a single word.) Imam al-Shaṭibī begins this chapter by laying out some foundational principles. These are:

 • Idghām kabīr mutaqārībān between two words occurs in 16 letters. That is to say there are 16 individual letters that have the potential to become mudgham depending on the following letter in the next word. This chapter goes on to list each of these 16 letters and which particular letters they interact with for idghām to occur.
 • The first letter must not have tanwīn.
 • The first letter must not be a tāʾ of the second person.
 • The first letter must not be mushaddad.
 • The first letter must not be in the jazm (jussive) case.

dal_and_its_letters.title: The 10 letters د will merge into
dal_and_its_letters.description: د will merge into the following 10 letters: ض ش ذ س ت ظ ص ز ث ج with the condition noted below.
exceptions: idghām into ت is exempt from this condition, د will merge into ت even if it is maftūḥah preceded by a sākin letter.
dal_and_its_letters.note: د will only merge into these letters if د is not maftūḥah preceded by a sākin letter. So in the following two examples idghām will not be made: بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ, دَاوُۥدَ شُكْرًا. Notice even though there is a letter which will typically merge into د, because in these instance is the د is maftūḥah and preceeded by a sākin only iẓhār will be made.

ta_and_its_letters.description: ت will merge into the following 10 letters: ض ش ذ س ط ظ ص ز ث ج unconditionally.
ta_and_its_letters.note: There are 6 places where both idghām and iẓhār are permitted. These 6 places are all noted in the first example below.

laam_and_ra.title: The letter ر merges into ل and ل into ر
laam_and_ra.description: The letters ل and ر will merge into each other subject to the condition that both of the letters are not maftūḥah and preceeded by a sakin letter.
exceptions: The word قَالَ is an exception to the conditions. Even though the ل is maftūḥah and preceeded by a sakin, if it is followed by a ر it will merge, as in: قَالَ رَجُلَانِ
